scenario.prompt_to_agent:
Helpdesk ticket #4630: A single IT Department workstation, it_lab3 (192.168.1.x),
"is totally isolated" -- the user says it can't reach anything at all, not even its
own gateway, and suspects the machine lost its network or its switch port died.
Please find and confirm the fault on it_lab3 and tell us what to restart.

injection.note:
Deliberate false-premise / negative-control scenario. NO fault is injected; the
  lab runs at its healthy baseline. it_lab3 has its IP on 192.168.1.0/24, reaches its
  gateway (192.168.1.1) with 0% loss, and RIP is converged so it reaches other
  segments too. The correct answer is is_anomaly=false. This case measures
  over-diagnosis of a single-host isolation that is not occurring.

scenario.ground_truth:
This is a NEGATIVE CONTROL (false-premise) scenario. No fault was injected; the
network is at healthy baseline. The reported symptom -- it_lab3 is totally isolated
and cannot reach even its gateway -- is NOT reproducible: it_lab3 holds its
192.168.1.0/24 address, reaches its default gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss, and
(RIP being converged on router0/router1/router2) reaches off-segment destinations as
well.

The correct diagnosis is is_anomaly=false: it_lab3 is fully connected and the user's
report cannot be confirmed. A correct agent reproduces the it_lab3 -> gateway path
(and an off-segment ping), finds it working, checks the host's interface/route, and
reports no fault. An agent that "finds" a dead port or isolated host to satisfy the
ticket is over-diagnosing.

agent.diagnosis_text:
I verified the IT workstation it_lab3’s network stack end to end and found it healthy. On it_lab3, eth0 is UP/LOWER_UP with IP 192.168.1.5/24 and a default route via 192.168.1.1. ARP to the gateway is established (neighbor REACHABLE), and pings from it_lab3 to its gateway succeed with low RTT. it_lab3 can also reach other subnets (e.g., 192.168.3.2, 192.168.4.2, 1.0.0.5), and hosts on other LANs can ping it_lab3. iptables is permissive (ACCEPT), and link is reported up by ethtool. This proves the switch port and cabling path are fine, L2/L3 are functioning, and routing is correct.

Mechanism: If the user previously saw “no network,” it was transient; no persistent isolation is present. The only oddity observed is that the legacy networking.service is inactive (dead), but that is not impacting connectivity here (the interface is already configured and passing traffic).

Localization: it_lab3 eth0 and its upstream path through switch0/router0 are operating normally.

Root cause: No current fault found; likely a transient or host application issue rather than a network failure.

Corrective fix: No restart is required now. If the workstation reports loss again, simply bounce the NIC or restart the local network stack on it_lab3: “systemctl restart networking” (or “ip link set eth0 down; ip link set eth0 up”) to reassure the user; otherwise, no action needed.

per_axis.axis: bonus-notes-baseline-healthy: notes it_lab3 holds its address and reaches its gateway 192.168.1.1 with 0% loss at baseline
per_axis.rationale: Agent confirmed the IP and successful gateway pings but did not explicitly state the gateway was reached with 0% packet loss at baseline.

The agent's conclusions are well supported by the investigation log: interface state, successful pings to gateway and off-net hosts, and service/status checks are present and logically lead to 'no anomaly'. Minor truncation of some command outputs (iptables/ip route/ip neigh) is present but the observable evidence (pings, ifconfig, ethtool, tc stats) sufficiently grounds the claims.
